title: Building a Life
stage: Partnership, home, money, and the if/when/whether of family

myths.myth: A spark is enough to build a life on.
myths.truth: Shared values and respect matter more than a spark.
myths.explanation: Compatibility outlasts chemistry.

myths.myth: People change after you commit.
myths.truth: Build with who someone is now, not who you hope they'll become.
myths.explanation: Hope isn't a plan.

myths.myth: Compromise means one person gives in.
myths.truth: Healthy commitment is mutual give-and-take.
myths.explanation: Lopsided 'compromise' is just losing.

myths.myth: Love conquers all incompatibility.
myths.truth: Love plus communication and aligned goals lasts.
myths.explanation: Love alone doesn't pay rent or raise kids.

myths.myth: There's an expiry date for getting married.
myths.truth: There's no deadline on your life.
myths.explanation: Timelines are social pressure, not facts.

myths.myth: A woman single past a certain age has 'failed'.
myths.truth: Being single can be a full, chosen, good life.
myths.explanation: Worth isn't a marital status.

myths.myth: Everyone must marry and have kids.
myths.truth: Marriage and children are choices, not obligations.
myths.explanation: A meaningful life takes many shapes.

myths.myth: Giving in to family pressure is just being a good child.
myths.truth: You can honour family and still choose your own path.
myths.explanation: Respect runs both ways.

myths.myth: Housework and childcare are 'naturally' the woman's job.
myths.truth: A home runs on shared, visible labour.
myths.explanation: Fairness isn't a favour.

myths.myth: A man who cooks or cleans is 'helping'.
myths.truth: It's his home too — it isn't 'helping'.
myths.explanation: 'Helping' implies it was really her job.

myths.myth: The mental load — remembering, planning — isn't real work.
myths.truth: Invisible labour is still labour.
myths.explanation: Sharing it is part of equality.

myths.myth: Earning more means doing less at home.
myths.truth: Income doesn't buy you out of partnership.
myths.explanation: A relationship isn't a payroll.

myths.myth: Marriage means you can't say no to sex.
myths.truth: Consent doesn't end at marriage.
myths.explanation: A spouse is a partner, not property.

myths.myth: What happens at home is private, even if it's harmful.
myths.truth: Abuse is never a private matter.
myths.explanation: Safety comes before 'log kya kahenge'.

myths.myth: Controlling a partner's money or movements is care.
myths.truth: That's coercive control — a form of abuse.
myths.explanation: Love doesn't cage.

myths.myth: Staying 'for the family' is always right.
myths.truth: Leaving harm protects everyone, including kids.
myths.explanation: Children learn from what they witness.

myths.myth: Marrying someone makes their family's rules yours.
myths.truth: Couples get to set their own boundaries.
myths.explanation: A new family unit is allowed to exist.

myths.myth: Keeping everyone happy is your job.
myths.truth: You can be kind and still say no.
myths.explanation: Boundaries aren't disrespect.

myths.myth: Elders are always right.
myths.truth: Respect doesn't mean never disagreeing.
myths.explanation: Wisdom and fallibility can coexist.

myths.myth: Conflict with in-laws means you've failed.
myths.truth: Negotiating differences is normal.
myths.explanation: Every joined family does it.

myths.myth: One partner should hold all the financial power.
myths.truth: Shared visibility and a say for both is healthier.
myths.explanation: Money power shouldn't be one-sided.

myths.myth: A homemaker doesn't 'contribute' financially.
myths.truth: Unpaid work has real economic value.
myths.explanation: Care work subsidises everything else.

myths.myth: Talking about separate accounts means you don't trust each other.
myths.truth: Clarity is care, not suspicion.
myths.explanation: Good fences make good partners too.

myths.myth: Debt and finances are too boring to discuss.
myths.truth: Money is a top cause of conflict — discuss it.
myths.explanation: Silence is expensive.

myths.myth: Having kids is the default; not wanting them is selfish.
myths.truth: Choosing whether to have children is valid either way.
myths.explanation: A wanted child and a chosen child-free life are both good.

myths.myth: Fertility lasts as long as you want it to.
myths.truth: Fertility changes with age for everyone.
myths.explanation: Facts help you plan, not panic.

myths.myth: If you can't conceive, you're 'broken'.
myths.truth: Infertility is common and not a verdict on worth.
myths.explanation: There are many paths and supports.

myths.myth: Family planning is only the woman's concern.
myths.truth: Whether and when to have kids is a shared decision.
myths.explanation: It takes two to plan.

myths.myth: A 'real' family needs a mother, a father and biological kids.
myths.truth: Families are built in many valid ways.
myths.explanation: Love and care make a family, not a template.

myths.myth: Adopted kids aren't 'really' yours.
myths.truth: Adoption builds full, real families.
myths.explanation: Parenting is about showing up, not genes.

myths.myth: Single men can't or shouldn't raise children.
myths.truth: Single men can adopt and parent well — though India's CARA rules don't yet let a single man adopt a girl child.
myths.explanation: Capability isn't gendered, even where the rules lag.

myths.myth: IVF, surrogacy or being child-free are things to hide.
myths.truth: How — or whether — you build a family is yours to own.
myths.explanation: Privacy is a choice; shame shouldn't be the default.

capstone.landing: Sticker-book spread of every Ch.7 sticker earned; the erased 'shoulds' of partnership and family glowing as ghosts under their truths; a 'Building Together' badge; Lensy pointing onward to Chapter 8, where the next child enters the loop.

canvasFeel: Adult/dark, wry-but-kind, and unafraid of the loaded ones — marriage-timeline pressure, the stigma around unmarried women, the mental load, consent within marriage, in-law boundaries, and many ways to build a family. g60 states the India CARA position carefully (single men can adopt, but not a girl child under current rules — verified June 2026).
